title: Simple Approximation and Derivative Free Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Sequential Monte Carlo on Path Measures
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Naive guidance drifts trajectories toward suboptimal modes; resampling at each step corrects them to the reward-tilted distribution.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left-to-right trajectories, orange resampled paths in right panel
description: Two framed panels share the same layout. Each shows noisy stochastic trajectories fanning out from a blue starting dot on the left to a grey ellipse of final samples on the right. Black solid and dashed paths are the base diffusion. Panel (a), Naïve Guidance, has light-blue guided paths with small blue arrows marking the guidance drift. The blue paths cluster in one region at the end, and a few large blue circles mark the final particles. Below it are a noisy face image labelled initial samples and a clean face labelled final samples, with math notation X_0^{(i),G} and X_T^{(i),G}. Panel (b), Unbiased Guidance via SMC, adds a vertical ellipse mid-trajectory labelled 'SMC resampling at each step'. Orange resampled paths appear, and the final ellipse has orange and blue circles. Panel captions sit underneath.
caption: Step-wise resampling corrects suboptimal guided generation toward the reward-tilted distribution. (a) In Naive Guidance, blue trajectories follow the guided diffusion $\dif X_t^G = \bigl(v(X_t^G,t)+{\color{blue}V(t)^2\nabla_x G(X_t^G,t)}\bigr)\dif t+ V(t)\dif W_t,$ whereas black trajectories follow the base diffusion without \(G\). (b) In our algorithm, we reweight and resample the generation trajectory to obtain consistent posterior samples from the reward-tilted distribution.
abstract: iffusion-based generative models increasingly rely on inference-time guidance, adding a drift term or reweighting mixture of experts, to improve sample quality on task-specific objectives. However, most existing techniques require repeated score or gradient evaluations, introducing bias, high computational overhead, or both. We introduce \texttt{URGE}, Unbiased Resampling via Girsanov Estimation, a derivative-free inference-time scaling algorithm that performs path-wise importance reweighting via a Girsanov change of measure. Instead of computing gradient-based particle weights in previous work, \texttt{URGE} attaches a simple multiplicative weight to each simulated trajectory and periodically resamples. No score, no Hessian, and no PDE evaluation is required. We establish an equivalence between path-wise and particle-wise SMC: the Girsanov path weight admits a backward conditional expectation that recovers the previous particle-level weights, guaranteeing that both schemes produce the same unbiased terminal law. Empirically, \texttt{URGE} outperforms existing inference-time guidance baselines on synthetic tests and diffusion-model benchmarks, achieving better generation quality, while being significantly simpler to implement and fully gradient-free.
